tape.title: Ferryman's log, 4 December
lines: Ferryman: Last crossing before the ice. Two passengers out, none back, which is normal for December.
Ferryman: The harbour master says the island keeps its own calendar. Thirteen nights before Christmas and twelve after.
Ferryman: Something left hoofprints on the slip. One hoof. Then a boot. Then a hoof. I've stopped writing these down. Mostly.

tape.title: Gary narrates
lines: Gary: We're on the Yule Isle, which is like a regular island but everyone here is very interested in whether you got new socks.
Gary: The lady at the shop said keep the fire lit all night. For warmth? No, she said. Not for warmth.
Gary: That's a birch switch on the doorstep. Just one. Leaning there. Like a message. Cut. Don't cut. Cut.

tape.title: Shepherd's tape, Twelfth Night
lines: Shepherd: The milk turned again. Third time this week. My wife says it's them, back up from under.
Shepherd: They saw all year, she says, and when they come up the tree's nearly through. Then it heals and they start over.
Shepherd: I asked what happens if they ever finish. She put another log on the fire and didn't answer.
